ci(smoke): test the latest detector under the real AWF path (#665)

* refactor(smoke): split Smoke Standalone Latest into three per-engine workflows

Replace the single smoke-standalone-latest.yml matrix workflow with three
per-engine workflows (smoke-{copilot,claude,codex}-standalone-latest.yml).
Each always resolves the newest published github/gh-aw-threat-detection
release (overridable via detector_tag) instead of the tag pinned by
production gh-aw, making it easy to diagnose and validate fixes per engine.
Update smoke.yml to dispatch the three workflows and refresh README docs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci(smoke): add latest-detector meta-workflow under real AWF path

Replace the earlier three direct-on-runner "standalone latest" smoke
workflows with a single meta-workflow (smoke-standalone-latest.yml) that:

  * resolves the newest prereleases of github/gh-aw and
    github/gh-aw-threat-detection (both overridable via inputs),
  * clones gh-aw at that prerelease and patches the hard-pinned
    DefaultThreatDetectVersion Go constant to the detector tag,
  * rebuilds the gh-aw compiler and recompiles the three
    smoke-<engine>-standalone.md workflows (SHA-pinned action mode
    matching the gh-aw prerelease),
  * pushes the recompiled locks to a throwaway branch and dispatches the
    real smoke-<engine>-standalone.lock.yml runs on it.

This exercises production's actual native gh-aw + AWF detection path with
only the detector version swapped, so each engine still runs as its own
independent AWF-backed smoke. Also wires smoke.yml's include_latest input
to the meta-workflow and refreshes the README.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci(smoke): harden latest-detector meta-workflow per review

Address three review findings in smoke-standalone-latest.yml:

* Ref resolution now falls back to the latest stable release when no
  prerelease exists (for both gh-aw and gh-aw-threat-detection), so the
  default and automatic runs no longer fail when a repo has no prerelease.
* Support tag/branch/SHA compiler refs by fetching the exact ref instead
  of `clone --branch`, and resolve a separate `action_tag` (always a real
  gh-aw release tag) for --action-tag, so a gh-aw branch or commit SHA
  still produces runnable, correctly SHA-pinned github/gh-aw-actions.
* Only delete a stale throwaway branch once all of its child smoke runs
  have completed, so a later meta-run can't delete a branch out from
  under an in-flight child (whose checkout would then fail).

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci(smoke): replace latest meta-workflow with PR-based refresh flow

Rework latest-detector smoke testing into a simpler, fully reviewable,
single-branch (main) model:

* Add committed smoke-<engine>-standalone-latest.{md,lock.yml} — latest
  counterparts of the pinned standalone smokes. They are dispatch-only
  plus a push trigger scoped to their own .lock.yml on main, so merging a
  refresh PR runs them automatically under the real gh-aw + AWF path.
* Add refresh-latest-smokes.yml: clones gh-aw at the newest (pre)release,
  patches DefaultThreatDetectVersion to the newest detector (pre)release,
  builds the compiler, recompiles the three -latest.md with SHA-pinned
  action mode, and opens/updates a PR with the regenerated locks.
* Remove the smoke-standalone-latest.yml meta-workflow and its
  throwaway-branch / cross-branch-dispatch machinery.
* Point smoke.yml's include_latest at the -latest.lock.yml files and
  refresh the README.

The committed -latest locks currently pin gh-aw v0.83.3 + detector main.
Only the detector version differs from production.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci(smoke): resolve newest version release, ignore rolling main

Fix two ref-resolution issues in refresh-latest-smokes.yml:

* Pick the newest release by publish date across prereleases AND stable
  releases, so a newer stable (e.g. gh-aw v0.83.4) wins over an older
  prerelease (v0.83.3), instead of always preferring the newest
  prerelease.
* Restrict resolution to semantic-version tags (^v[0-9]), ignoring the
  detector's rolling `main` prerelease tag. `main` is re-published in
  place, which would make the pinned locks non-reproducible; the newest
  real detector version tag is v0.3.1.

Regenerate the committed latest smoke locks accordingly: gh-aw v0.83.4,
detector v0.3.1, github/gh-aw-actions/setup pinned to v0.83.4.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci(smoke): add scope choice (standard / standard+latest / latest)

Replace smoke.yml's boolean include_latest input with a `scope` choice so
the top-level Smoke workflow can run the pinned smokes only, both pinned
and latest, or the latest-detector smokes on their own. Gate each
dispatch step on the selected scope.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

@@ -0,0 +1,86 @@
+---
+description: Smoke test workflow that validates Claude engine execution with the released threat-detect binary
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+    paths:
+      - .github/workflows/smoke-claude-standalone-latest.lock.yml
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+  pull-requests: read
+  actions: read
+name: Smoke Claude Standalone Latest
+engine:
+  id: claude
+  max-turns: 20
+  bare: true
+model: claude-sonnet-4.6
+strict: false
+features:
+  gh-aw-detection: true
+network:
+  allowed:
+    - defaults
+    - github
+tools:
+  bash:
+    - "*"
+  github:
+    mode: gh-proxy
+runtimes:
+  go:
+    version: "1.26"
+checkout:
+  fetch-depth: 1
+safe-outputs:
+  allowed-domains: [default-safe-outputs]
+  threat-detection:
+    continue-on-error: false
+    engine:
+      id: claude
+      env:
+        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: claude-sonnet-4.6
+  create-issue:
+    expires: 2h
+    close-older-issues: true
+    close-older-key: "smoke-claude-standalone-latest"
+    labels: [automation, testing]
+timeout-minutes: 15
+---
+
+# Smoke Test: Claude Engine Validation (Standalone Detector)
+
+> **Generated / latest-detector variant.** This is the *latest* counterpart of
+> `smoke-claude-standalone.md`. Its `.lock.yml` is regenerated by the
+> `refresh-latest-smokes.yml` workflow against the newest gh-aw and
+> gh-aw-threat-detection (pre)releases. Do **not** run a plain `gh aw compile`
+> on it — that would revert the patched detector version. It runs on manual
+> dispatch and whenever its `.lock.yml` changes on `main`.
+
+Keep outputs concise.
+
+This workflow validates the Claude engine while exercising the **native external
+threat-detect path** (`features: gh-aw-detection: true`). gh-aw downloads the
+published `threat-detect` binary from the `github/gh-aw-threat-detection` releases
+and runs it under AWF, replacing the script-generated container sibling.
+
+## Test Requirements
+
+1. Use GitHub tools to read the latest 2 pull requests in `${{ github.repository }}` and record their numbers and titles only.
+2. Use bash to run `make test` in `${{ github.workspace }}` and verify it succeeds.
+3. Use bash to create a minimal artifacts directory under `/tmp/gh-aw/smoke-claude-standalone-${{ github.run_id }}` with:
+   - `aw-prompts/prompt.txt`
+   - `agent_output.json`
+4. Use bash to run `./bin/threat-detect --version`; if the binary does not exist, run `make build` first.
+5. Use bash to write a concise status file at `/tmp/gh-aw/agent/smoke-claude-standalone-${{ github.run_id }}.txt`.
+
+## Output
+
+Always create an issue titled `Smoke Test: Claude Standalone Latest - ${{ github.run_id }}` with:
+- ✅ or ❌ for each test
+- Overall status: PASS or FAIL
+- Run URL: `${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}`
+- Timestamp

commits.message:
fix(smoke): drop push trigger from latest smokes to unblock dispatch (#671)

* fix(smoke): drop push trigger from latest smokes to unblock dispatch

The smoke-*-standalone-latest workflows declared a `push` trigger, which
caused gh-aw to generate a `pre_activation` team-membership gate
(required roles: admin,maintainer,write). When dispatched from smoke.yml,
the actor is `github-actions[bot]` (permission `none`), so activation
failed. The non-latest smokes use only schedule + workflow_dispatch and
have no such gate.

Remove the `push` trigger from the three `-latest` .md sources and their
compiled .lock.yml files, along with the now-unused `pre_activation` job
and all references to it. Update refresh-latest-smokes.yml docs/PR body to
reflect that latest smokes are now dispatched (via smoke.yml or manually)
rather than push-triggered on merge.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* chore(smoke): recompile latest smoke locks with gh-aw v0.83.4

Regenerate the three smoke-*-standalone-latest.lock.yml files with the
canonical gh-aw v0.83.4 compiler (detector version constant patched to
v0.3.1, matching refresh-latest-smokes.yml and the committed pins) instead
of the previous hand-edits. This corrects the frontmatter_hash and lets the
compiler emit the simplified concurrency group for the now push-free
trigger, while preserving the detector pin, action SHAs, container digests,
and the COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN secret.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

ci: push refreshed smoke locks with workflows-permitted token (#677)

* ci: push refreshed smoke locks with workflows-permitted token

Persist GH_AW_GITHUB_TOKEN via actions/checkout so the git push in the
Refresh Latest Smokes workflow can update the smoke `.lock.yml` files
under .github/workflows/. The built-in GITHUB_TOKEN (github-actions[bot]
GitHub App) is refused for workflow-file changes without the `workflows`
permission.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>

* ci: replace lock-refresh workflows with read-only version check

Add `gh-aw-version-check.yml`, a daily read-only workflow that verifies
each compiled `*.lock.yml` tracks the right versions per category
(standard -> latest stable gh-aw; standalone smoke -> latest gh-aw
release/prerelease; standalone latest -> latest gh-aw + latest detector
release/prerelease). On drift it opens/updates a single tracking issue
pointing at the update-workflow-versions skill; it builds and compiles
nothing and needs only `contents: read` + `issues: write`.

Delete `refresh-latest-smokes.yml` and `update-gh-aw.yml`, which pushed
regenerated locks and required a `workflows`-permitted token.

Add `scripts/check-workflow-versions.sh` (the read-only check) and
`scripts/recompile-workflows.sh` (regenerates locks per category,
patching the detector constant for the latest workflows), plus the
`update-workflow-versions` skill documenting the human-reviewed
regeneration flow. Update README and smoke workflow references.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Co-authored-by: David Slater <12449447+davidslater@users.noreply.github.com>
